clue.text: Fringe benefit perhaps available in some industries?

definitions.text: Fringe benefit perhaps available in some industries?

parts.words: Fringe benefit perhaps available in some industries?
parts.note: an extra advantage that comes as a side result of a manufacturing process, read as a perk from a factory

explanation.surface: A question about which industries offer perks to employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringe benefit' suggests a job perk; it is really any secondary result made alongside the main product.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary result produced incidentally alongside the main output can loosely be called a fringe benefit.

clue.text: Jazz award black picked up, on piano

indicators.note: in a down entry, picked up means lifted, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour awarded in the UK
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A jazz musician wins an award, and a black performer collects it at the keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns OBE + B into BEBO; 'on' puts P after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebop is a fast, complex style of jazz developed in the 1940s.

clue.text: So it was ages before anyone wrote

definitions.text: So it was ages before anyone wrote

parts.words: So it was ages before anyone wrote
parts.note: sounds like a complaint about a slow correspondent, but describes the era before writing existed

explanation.definitionFit: The period before written records is by definition the time preceding recorded history.

clue.text: Tragically, killer hiding in forest escaped

indicators.note: the words forest escaped conceal the answer within their run of letters

explanation.surface: A murderer has escaped by hiding out in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: Orestes, in Greek tragedy, kills his mother Clytemnestra to avenge his father.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek tragedy this hero avenges his father by murdering his mother, so he is a tragic killer.

clue.text: At university, what Jack did appears inspired

parts.note: UP means in residence at university, as in going up to Oxford
a car jack raises a vehicle, so what it did is lifted

explanation.surface: A student named Jack seems inspired by his time at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a person's name; it is the tool that lifts a car.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel uplifted is to have one's spirits raised, much as being inspired does.

clue.text: Indelible impression made by military parade

definitions.meaning: a permanent design inked into the skin
an evening display of marching bands and troops, like the Edinburgh one

explanation.surface: A permanent mark left by watching soldiers march past.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a permanent ink design on skin and a military display such as the Edinburgh one.

clue.text: Type of wine, one missed by GP? Nothing can replace it

indicators.note: the clue says the zero takes the place of the missing numeral one

parts.note: a GP, general practitioner, is a doctor or medic
the Roman numeral for one is I
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A doctor misses a type of wine, with nothing to replace it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed by' says the I goes from MEDIC; 'can replace it' says O takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a Bordeaux region whose red wines are named after it.

clue.text: Playwright increasingly including deception

indicators.note: one word takes the other inside it, as a container

parts.note: more and more, so MORE
a lie is a deception

explanation.surface: A dramatist whose plays involve more and more trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the great seventeenth-century French comic dramatist, author of Tartuffe.

clue.text: Pair of dungarees, unpleasantly odoriferous at first

indicators.note: take the opening letter of each of these three words

explanation.surface: A pair of overalls that smell unpleasant from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a set of two, a synonym for a pair.

clue.text: Columns needing punctuation and English edited

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark

indicators.note: editing reworks the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: An editor fixes punctuation in columns of English text.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonnade is a row of columns supporting a roof.

clue.text: Note in dialogue of Eastenders meaning to inspire?

indicators.note: Cockney speech of East London, where EastEnders is set, turns a th sound into v

parts.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in

explanation.surface: A soap opera's dialogue is meant to inspire viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in Cockney East London, where 'th' is often said as 'v'. A breve is a long note in music.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a musical note equal in length to two semibreves.

clue.text: Almost too well-lit? That's inappropriate for this bird

indicators.note: letters put somewhere unsuitable are out of their proper order
the word too loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A bird that likes darkness would find somewhere too brightly lit unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts TOO to TO; 'inappropriate' rearranges TO + WELLLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The little owl is a small European owl species, so it fits as this bird.

clue.text: Reason for ignoring taxman, after which one's committed?

definitions.meaning: the purpose of not filing a tax form, read humorously
the stage beyond which turning back is impossible

explanation.surface: Why someone ignores the tax office, past which they cannot back out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the stage past which going back is impossible, punned on a missing tax return.

clue.text: Old man, true to form, keeping right up-to date? Certainly

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold another letter inside
the letters are shaped into a new form

explanation.surface: An old man, true to character, keeps right up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to form' rearranges OLDMANTRUE; 'keeping' puts R among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely modern is more than merely current, hence certainly up to date.

clue.text: Approach status of tennis star, then deteriorate

parts.note: to approach is to go to
top tennis players are given a seeding in tournaments

explanation.surface: A tennis player approaches top ranking, then goes into decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that run to seed stop producing, so the idiom means to decline or deteriorate.

clue.text: Someone shirking in 27, or loyal chap?

definitions.meaning: American slang for a shirker, Des Moines being in the US
a good-as-gold, reliable fellow, a brick being a dependable friend

explanation.surface: An American idler, or perhaps a loyal friend?
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is the answer to 27-across, an American city, so US slang applies. A 'brick' is old British slang for a dependable friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is US slang for someone who idles on the job, and can be read as gold plus brick, a sterling fellow.

clue.text: Sleeping quarters given to a woman

parts.note: a berth is a bunk on a ship or train

explanation.surface: A woman is given a sleeping cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a woman's name.

clue.text: Woman wearing these looks good to boss!

definitions.text: Woman wearing these looks good to boss!

parts.words: Woman wearing these looks good to boss!
parts.note: plays on the idiom for the dominant partner, who is said to wear these garments

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says whoever wears the leg garments in a household is the one in charge.

clue.text: Source of squeaks a rodent originally caught by cat

indicators.note: the cat holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat

indicators.note: take the opening letter of rodent

explanation.surface: A mouse squeaks when caught by a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives R from rodent; 'caught by' puts A + R inside LYNX.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box in the throat produces sounds, including squeaks.

clue.text: Maybe do allow a brief message

parts.note: do, as in do-re-mi, is a note of the scale
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Perhaps we should permit a short message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a verb; it is the musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card for a short written message.

clue.text: Meaning to mature, then going off course

parts.note: the drift of an argument is its meaning
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Meaning to grow up but straying from the path.
explanation.definitionFit: Driftage is deviation of a ship or aircraft from its set course by drifting.

clue.text: Appearing distant in the past, runs in, causing mix-up

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the phrase

parts.note: far ago means long in the past
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Something from long ago runs into a confusing jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused mixture or hotchpotch.

clue.text: Man in party circumventing rules set up

indicators.note: in a down entry the whole thing is read upwards
going around, so the party surrounds the rules

parts.note: a do is a party
laws are rules

explanation.surface: A man at a party is getting around the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circumventing' puts LAWS in DO to make DLAWSO; 'set up' turns it to OSWALD.
explanation.definitionFit: A male given name of Old English origin, borne by a Northumbrian king and saint, so a man is a fair definition by example.

clue.text: Illegal pawn move made, so having to start again

definitions.meaning: a chess pawn can never move backwards to its starting square
returning to the very beginning of a task

explanation.surface: A chess player makes a banned pawn move and must restart.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means returning to the starting point, read literally as a pawn retreating to its original square.

clue.text: Characteristic attitudes, the ones European promoted

indicators.note: in a down entry, promotion raises the letter to the top

parts.note: those means the ones

explanation.surface: A European colleague promoted for having the right outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or set of attitudes of a community.

clue.text: Habitually stress the idea I can't clue, perhaps?

indicators.note: signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A frustrated setter complains about failing to write a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To inculcate is to instil an idea by persistent repetition.

clue.text: Signal and hint left ignored

indicators.note: the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a clue is a hint

explanation.surface: A signal and a hint were both disregarded.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a signal for an actor or performer to begin.

clue.text: Character beginning to read Psalm 119

definitions.meaning: a letter of an alphabet, here the Hebrew one
Psalm 119 is an acrostic whose first section is headed by this first Hebrew letter

explanation.surface: A believer opens the Bible to read Psalm 119.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet and heads the first stanza of Psalm 119.

clue.text: Prepared to make a proposal concerning union procedure

definitions.text: Prepared to make a proposal concerning union procedure

parts.words: Prepared to make a proposal concerning union procedure
parts.note: sounds like a trade union meeting, but describes a man going down on one knee to propose marriage

explanation.definitionFit: A traditional marriage proposal is made on bended knee, so the suitor went down on one knee.

clue.text: Loose ends, some involving Iowa's capital? Yes

definitions.text: Loose ends, some involving Iowa's capital? Yes

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around another letter
loose letters are free to move into a new order
the capital, that is first, letter of Iowa

explanation.surface: Asks whether loose ends involve Iowa's capital city, answering yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' rearranges ENDSSOME; 'capital' gives I, which 'involving' places inside. Des Moines is the state capital of Iowa.
explanation.definitionFit: Des Moines is the state capital of Iowa, so the whole clue describes it.
